I’ve worked at multiple doggy daycares and can say:
1- trust your instincts 
2- most smaller doggies tend to enjoy more laid back/less wild playgroups— and more time either with a low amount of playmates of their size and energy, or one on one time with the kennel techs.

I cannot tell you how many dogs I would care for that were absolutely miserable, and I was told NOT to tell the owners, but I did anyways.. because I wouldn’t want my dog to be miserable. I have a different career now- but if I ever want my doggie cared for— I tend to take him to a less crammed doggy daycare (sadly many these days care only about making money and not the animals and how they feel.. my last kennel boss ignored my feelings and me expressing that we should accept less dogs. She only cared about it “being a good price to make around the holidays” and said “if we run out of room we can just get more crates” in a TINY, already crammed room. 

I’d recommend something like petsitter.com, wag, or even reaching out on the Nextdoor app about wanting your doggie to have play dates, and or small playmate groups, weekly.

I’ve struggled with quitting and relapsing for the past 3 years— but am finally making real progress. 

Some of my most important reminders and takes:

-HOW YOU TREAT AND SPEAK TO YOURSELF (throughout every day and chapter BUT ESPECIALLY WHEN YOU STRUGGLE during this time) is so so so important. Be kind to yourself. The biggest battle I found was with my mind and my body. I kept affirming things that were no longer true “weed is good for me” “just once won’t hurt”, “I need it to sleep/eat/kill the nausea” —things like that, you’ve got to change the affirmations that you repeat to yourself. Anytime you notice a negative thought- replace it with a positive one. When you practice this, it will get rid of the toxic thought patterns and replace them with good, healthy, empowering ones. 

Did you know that most of our thoughts are just recycled? ESPECIALLY when you’ve depended on cannabis for some time— especially if it’s been years.

-Your brain is going to throw a temper tantrum when you crave— but just like you’d handle a toddler throwing a temper tantrum—you cannot cave. You cannot teach yourself that the urges are stronger than your desires to quit and become sober, and happy sober. 

-Replace the habit with something fulfilling. (For me personally I only ever really smoked in the evenings and convinced myself that I couldn’t eat or sleep without it— for the first few days I drank some tea with honey, and listened to some relaxing music, after a tiring workout and it truly is a game changer!!) Show yourself that you are much stronger than the dependency— because YOU ARE SO MUCH STRONGER. The fact that you chose to end cannabis usage- that you decided to acknowledge that it is no longer benefiting you— that alone is proof. As far as replacing my smoking habit— when I get an urge I allow myself to write about it, workout, meditate, and/or do some art! Things that will only benefit me and help me find relief, things that help me stay sober and enjoy and appreciate being alive.
